statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is in the low band, below the block threshold.
recommendation: Tail is 18% with NQ holding a narrow two-sided overnight band and retracements still freely available, although the contract is sitting at the low end of that band as the Bank of Japan statement window approaches. The narrow evidence-based danger window covers the 13:00-14:30 UTC quarterly expiration cash open, the only projected block-band hour of the next 24. The Bank of Japan statement window at 02:30-03:30 UTC, Governor Ueda's 06:30 UTC press conference and the 20:00 UTC expiration settlement are treated as conditional checkpoints rather than current blocks. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures drift to the low of a narrow overnight band as the Bank of Japan statement window opens on quarterly expiration day
body: NQ is trading near 29,657.75, down about 85 points or 0.29%, at the low of a 29,657.75-29,728.50 overnight band as of 01:15 UTC; a second delayed feed reads 29,662.50 within the same band. The contract has given back roughly 38 points since the 00:17 UTC observation, but the move is a slow drift rather than an impulse: the band spans only about 71 points, or 0.24%, and the session has been two-sided. Sitting at a session extreme is a mild amplifier, yet on its own, without shallow pullbacks or repeated extension after failed retracements, it does not establish the persistent one-way structure that denies mean reversion. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed on 17 September after a broad recovery session in which the Nasdaq Composite gained 1.7%, the S&P 500 1.1% and the Dow 0.6%, reversing much of the decline that followed the Federal Reserve's 25 basis point increase to a 3.75%-4.00% target range on 16 September, approved by a 12-0 vote. Cross-asset evidence is constructive rather than stressed: the VIX fell 12.82% to 15.44 against a 17.20 prior close, the 10-year Treasury yield eased about six basis points to 4.947% from 5.006%, and WTI crude is near $101.24 in a $100.76-$101.33 band. The Federal Reserve H.15 release still shows 16 September constant-maturity readings of 4.74% at two years and 5.01% at ten years. In Asia the Nikkei 225 is trading at 64,686.35, up 0.86%, with USD/JPY at 156.21 in a 155.86-156.30 range. That firm Tokyo tape against a softer NQ is a mild cross-asset conflict, which reduces directional conviction rather than mechanically raising Tail. Two scheduled catalysts define the next 24 hours. The Bank of Japan concludes its two-day meeting today with the statement due in a 02:30-03:30 UTC window that carries no fixed release time, followed by Governor Ueda's press conference at 06:30 UTC; rate futures imply roughly 99% odds of a move to 1.25%, so the asymmetric surprise is a hold or a shift in tightening-pace guidance rather than the hike itself, with yen-carry the credible transmission channel. Today is also the September quarterly expiration, with index options settling on the special opening quotation at the 13:30 UTC cash open against roughly 6.2 trillion dollars of expiring U.S. options exposure, which is why the 13:00-14:30 UTC window anchors the danger window. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was read but is not usable this run: it was collected at 23:08 UTC, is beyond the 90-minute freshness limit, and reports a partial collection with the futures and calendar sections unavailable. Neither scheduled catalyst is treated as observed structure at this time.

lookbackSummary: The 24 hours to 00:00 UTC are fully covered by published Claude assessments. Tail ranged between 17% and 26%, peaking at 26% in the 13:00 UTC hour around Thursday's U.S. cash open and easing steadily to 17% by the 00:00 UTC hour after futures reopened. Stress fell throughout the period from 71% to 40% as post-Fed repricing resolved in an orderly way and implied volatility decayed. The dominant mode was recorded as trend-up through most of the cash session, reflecting a persistent but measured upside recovery, and returned to normal once the evening band formed.
outlookSummary: The projected path holds 18% through the current pre-decision hour, then steps into the watch band as the Bank of Japan statement window opens at 02:30 UTC. It peaks for the Asian session at 23% in the 03:00 UTC statement hour, eases into the 05:00 UTC lull, and returns to 23% around Governor Ueda's 06:30 UTC press conference, the structurally multi-stage part of the sequence. A 19% floor follows through the European mid-morning. The only conditional block-band reading of 25% falls in the 13:00 UTC hour, which stacks August Industrial Production at 13:15 UTC, a Federal Reserve speaker at 13:30 UTC and the quarterly expiration cash open at 13:30 UTC; that hour anchors the danger window, which closes at 14:30 UTC. A second conditional step to 23% covers the 19:00 UTC witching hour and the 20:00 UTC expiration settlement, after which equity index futures close for the weekend at 21:00 UTC and the path falls to a residual floor near 13%. Stress tracks the same shape between 30% and 52%. Every forecast hour beyond the current one describes conditional risk, not observed structure.
